chapters.title: 1. The last train
paragraphs: The last train had already left when Mara reached the station. She stood under the clock and looked at the empty platform. The next train would not arrive until morning.
She could walk home, but the road through the woods was dark. There was still a light in the little station café. Mara pushed the door open.
An old man sat by the window with a cup of tea. The woman behind the counter was putting clean plates on a shelf.
“You look cold,” the woman said. “There is some soup left.”
Mara took off her wet coat and sat down. For the first time that evening, she stopped looking at her watch.

chapters.title: 2. A name on a card
paragraphs: The old man turned towards her. He held a small card with a name and a telephone number on it.
“My daughter is coming to meet me,” he said. “But my phone has stopped working. Could you call her?”
Mara took out her phone. A woman answered almost at once. She was waiting at the other entrance to the station, on the far side of the tracks.
“Tell her to stay there,” said the man. “I know the way.”
But when he tried to stand up, his heavy bag fell to the floor. Mara picked it up and offered to walk with him. They thanked the woman in the café and went outside together.

chapters.title: 3. The way home
paragraphs: A narrow bridge joined the two platforms. From the top, Mara could see a car beside the other entrance. A woman in a red scarf was waving.
The man waved back. He walked more quickly now, and Mara carried his bag down the steps.
His daughter thanked her and asked where she was going. When Mara explained that she had missed the last train, the woman smiled.
“We pass your street on our way home. Come with us.”
As the car left the station, Mara looked back. The café light was still on. She had missed her train, but the evening no longer felt like a mistake.
